predecessors.name: Liang dynasty
predecessors.text: Jiangling, the seat of Emperor Yuan of Liang until Western Wei sacked it in winter 554-January 555

successors.name: Sui dynasty
successors.text: Jiangling and the Western Liang territory in central Hubei

ledger.x: 555: Xiao Cha is set up at Jiangling.
560: the Western Liang gets half of Xiao Zhuang's territory.
561: the Western Liang cedes it to the Chen.
571: the Northern Zhou gives the Western Liang three provinces.
587: two Western Liang officials surrender to the Chen.
587: the Sui abolishes the Western Liang.

wars.name: Chen-Wang Lin war
wars.outcome: The Chen beat Wang Lin in spring 560 and split Xiao Zhuang's territory with the Western Liang, which ceded its half in spring 561.

wars.name: Sui annexation of the Western Liang
wars.outcome: No fighting is recorded: Sui general Cui Hongdu moved on Jiangling, two Western Liang officials surrendered part to the Chen, and the Sui abolished the state.

certainty.note: A small enclave round Jiangling whose edges with the Chen, the Zhou and the Qi are approximate; the page gives no boundary.
